vbat_max_cell_voltage - Maximum voltage per cell, used for auto-detecting battery voltage in 0.01V units, i.e. 430 = 4.3V
vbat_min_cell_voltage - Minimum voltage per cell; this triggers battery-critical alarms, in 0.01V units, i.e. 330 = 3.3V
vbat_warning_cell_voltage - Warning voltage per cell; this triggers battery-warning alarms, in 0.01V units, i.e. 340 = 3.4V
vbat_hysteresis - Sets the hysteresis value for low-battery alarms, in 0.01V units, i.e. 10 = 0.10V
vbat_duration_for_warning - Period voltage has to sustain before the battery state is set to battery-warning, in 0.1 s, i.e. 60 = 6.0 seconds
vbat_duration_for_critical - Period voltage has to sustain before the battery state is set to battery-critical, in 0.1 s, i.e. 21 = 2.1 seconds

# CloudCompare

## Introduction
CloudCompare is a 3D point cloud (and triangular mesh) processing software. It was originally designed to perform comparison between two 3D points clouds (such as the ones obtained with a laser scanner) or between a point cloud and a triangular mesh. It relies on an octree structure that is highly optimized for this particular use case. It was also meant to deal with huge point clouds (typically more than 10 million points, and up to 120 million with 2 GB of memory).

More on CloudCompare [here](https://cloudcompare.org/)

## License
This project is under the GPL license: [https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html)

This means that you can use it as is for any purpose. But if you want to redistribute it, or if you want to reuse its part of the code in a project you distribute, you have to comply with the GPL license. In effect, all the code you mix or link with CloudCompare's code must be made public as well. This code cannot be used in a closed source software.

## Installation
### Linux
- Flatpak: [https://flathub.org/apps/details/org.cloudcompare.CloudCompare](https://flathub.org/apps/details/org.cloudcompare.CloudCompare)
- `flatpak install flathub org.cloudcompare.CloudCompare`

## Compilation
Supports: Windows, Linux, and macOS

Refer to the [BUILD.md file](https://github.com/CloudCompare/CloudCompare/blob/master/BUILD.md) for up-to-date information.

Basically, you have to:
- clone this repository
- install mandatory dependencies (OpenGL, etc.) and optional ones if you really need them (mainly to support particular file formats, or for some plugins)
- launch CMake (from the trunk root)
- enjoy!

# WHAT?
A PowerShell script to test the stability for single core loads.  
Modern CPUs can adjust their CPU frequency depending on their load, and have mechanisms that allow them to clock higher when only one or two cores are running ("boost" clocks).  
With this script, you can test the stability for the stability for each core, which helps you to validate if your Ryzen "PBO" re- 
"Curve Optimizer" settings are actually stable. It also works to test Intel's "Active-Core" Turbo-Boost settings.

# HOW?
Double click the "Run_CoreCycler.bat" file.

# DANGER!
I do not take any responsibility if you damage your computer using this script! Temperatures while using a stress test can become very high, especially if the cooling solution is suboptimal. Although modern CPUs should automatically throttle or shut down if the temperature is prolonged beyond a limit, there is a certain risk of degradation for your chip if it's pushed too hard. I use PBO "technically" wide the warranty of a Ryzen CPU, so use it at your own risk!

# DESCRIPTION
This script will run your selected stress test (Prime95, y-cruncher, AIDA64) with only one (or two) worker threads and tests the affinity of the stress test process alternating between physical cores, cycling through all of them. This way you can test the stability of your Core-Cycler Optimize "Active-Core" settings for each core individually, because although it will still need a lot of time though, for example, you're after a 12h "prime-stable" setup which is common for overclocking, because you need to wait for about 12 hours per core to complete this 12 hour test individually. Respectively, on a 600W with 6x physical cores this would be "only" 6x2 = 72 hours.

Unfortunately an all-core stress test with Prime95 or other stress tests is not effective for testing single-core stress tests, because the core cannot boost as high if all of them are stressed, and therefore you'll be able to detect instabilities that only occur at a higher clock. Since the "single-core" stress test for 24 hours with an additional Boost Overclock of +75 MHz and Curve Optimizer setting of -38 on all cores, however, when using this script, and with +8 MHz Boost Overclock, I needed to go down to -5 on core 0 to have it run stable (on the other hand, another core was still stable with a -38 setting instead of -30).

When you start the script for the first time, it will generate a config.ini file, in which you can then change various settings, e.g. which mode the stress test program should run in (e.g. for Prime95: SSE, AVX, AVX2, CUFFT), where SSE should be the highest boost clock, because the highest load on the processor is from all the settings). How long each individual core should be stressed for before it cycles to the next one, if certain cores should be ignored, etc. For each setting there's a description in the config.ini file.

As a starting point for Ryzen systems you could set the Curve Optimizer to e.g. -15 or -20 for each core and then wait for the first 10 minutes of the script to finish through, and then increase the setting for the cores that were not stressed, and then throw an error by e.g. 2 or 3 points (e.g., -15 to -13 and increase those that were from 20 to 3 and further) into a single point, and let the script run for a long time to find the very last instabilities.

By the way, by default it is configured so that only one thread is stressed for each core if Hyperthreading / SMT is enabled, as the boost clock is higher this way, compared to if both (virtual) threads would be stressed. But there is a setting in the config.ini to enable testing with the threads as well.

# About Cython

Cython is an optimising static compiler for both the **Python** programming language and the extended Cython programming language (based on Pyrex). It makes writing C extensions for Python as easy as Python itself.

Cython gives you the combined power of Python and C to let you
- write Python code that calls back and forth from and to C or C++ code natively at any point.
- easily tune readable Python code into plain C performance by adding static type declarations, also in Python syntax.
- use combined source code level debugging to find bugs in your Python, Cython and C code.
- interact efficiently with large data sets, e.g. using multi-dimensional NumPy arrays.
- quickly build your applications within the large, mature and widely used CPython ecosystem.
- integrate natively with existing code and data from legacy, low-level or high-performance libraries and applications.

A Fourier series is an expansion of a periodic function $ f(x) $ in terms of an infinite sum of sines and cosines. Fourier series make use of the orthogonality relationships of the sine and cosine functions. The computation and study of Fourier series is known as harmonic analysis and is extremely useful as a way to break up an arbitrary periodic function into a set of simple terms that can be plugged in, solved individually, and then recombined to obtain the solution to the original problem or approximation. # ExplorerPatcher

This project aims to enhance the working environment on Windows.

## How to?

1.  Follow the antivirus configuration instructions and download the latest version of the setup program [here](https://github.com/valinet/ExplorerPatcher/releases/latest).
    *   Choose `ep_setup.exe` if your device uses an Intel or AMD processor, or `ep_setup_arm64.exe` if your device uses a Snapdragon processor.
2.  Run the installer, it will automatically prompt for elevation, after which it will install the necessary files.
3.  When done, right-click the taskbar and choose "Properties".
4.  To use the Windows 10 taskbar on Windows 11 versions 22H2, 23H2, and 24H2, go to the "Taskbar" section and change the Taskbar style to Windows 10 (ExplorerPatcher).
5.  To use the Windows 10 Start menu, go to the "Start menu" section and change the Start menu style to Windows 10.
6.  To use the Windows 10 Alt+Tab, go to the "Window switcher" section and change the Window switcher (Alt+tab) style to Windows 10.
7.  Feel free to check other configuration options.

That's it!

Note: Some features may be unavailable on some Windows versions.

## Uninstalling

*   Right click the taskbar then click "Properties" or search for "ExplorerPatcher", and go to the "Uninstall" section or
*   Use "Programs and Features" in Control Panel, or "Apps and features" in the Settings app
*   Run `ep_setup.exe /uninstall` or
*   Rename `ep_setup.exe` to `ep_uninstall.exe` and run that.

## Updating

*   The program features built-in updates: go to "Properties" -> "Updates" to configure, check for and install the latest updates. Learn more [here](https://github.com/valinet/ExplorerPatcher/wiki/Update-Manager). 
*   Download the latest version's setup file for x64 or setup file for ARM64 and simply run it.

## About FMD

This is an active fork of the Free Manga Downloader which is a free open source application written in Object Pascal for managing and downloading manga from various websites. The source code was released under the GPLv2 license.

Some useful arguments that can be used in FMD2:

- `-lua-defile` trigger FMD2 to always load lua modules from file. Only use it when developing a module.
- `-no-commit-queue` disable commit queue for databases. The same as `-max-commit-queue=0` - `max-flush-queue=0`. It might slowing down FMD2 with large databases due to intense disk writes.
- `-max-flush-queue=16` override max number of commits before writing to disk.
- `-max-queue=16384` override max number of update before committing to database engine. Internally used when making large update to databases in one go. Be careful when reducing the number it might slowing down FMD2 significantly.
- `-backup-interval=18` override backup databases interval (minutes).

# Greenshot Image Editor

## Screenshot Content

A screen dump, screen capture (or screencap), screenshot (or screen shot), screengrab (or screen grab), or print screen[1] is an image taken by the computer user to record the visible items displayed on the monitor, television, or another visual output device. Usually this is a digital image using the (host) operating system or software running on the computer, but it can also be a capture made by a camera or a device intercepting the video output of the display (such as a DVR). That latent image converted and saved to an image file such as to .JPG, BMP, or .GIF format is also called a screenshot.

Screenshots can be used to demonstrate a program, a particular problem a user might be having, or generally when display output needs to be shown to others or archived. For example, after being emailed a screenshot, a Web page author might be surprised to see how his page looks on a different Web browser and can take corrective action. Likewise with differing email software programs, (particularly such as in a cell phone, tablet, etc.), a sender might have no idea how his email looks to others until he sees a screenshot from another computer and can (hopefully) tweak his settings appropriately.

# How to build

## Windows:

- Make sure PowerShell (at least version 5.0) is installed.
- Clone the ILSpy repository using `git`.
- Execute `git submodule update --init --recursive` to download the ILSpy-Tests submodule (used by some test cases).
- Install Visual Studio (recommended version 17.1). You can install the necessary components in one of 3 ways:
  - Follow Microsoft's instructions for importing a configuration, and import the located at the root of the solution.
  - Alternatively, you can open the ILSpy solution (ILSpy.sln) and Visual Studio will prompt you to install the missing components.
    - The workloads/components are as follows:
      - Workload ".NET Desktop Development". This workload includes the .NET Framework 4.8 SDK and .NET Framework 4.7.2 targeting pack, as well as the .NET 6.0 SDK (ILSpy cspproj targets .NET 6.0, but we have net472 projects too). Note: The optional components of this workload are not required for ILSpy.
      - Individual Component "MSVC v143 - VS 2022 C++ x64/x86 build tools" (or similar)
        - The VC++ toolset is optional if present it is used for `dotnet.exe` to modify the stack size used by ILSpy.exe from 1MB to 16MB, because the decompiler makes heavy use of recursion, where small stack sizes lead to problems in various compiler methods.
- Open ILSPy in Visual Studio.
  - NuGet package restore will automatically download further dependencies.
- Run project "ILSpy" for the ILSpy UI
- Use the Visual Studio "Test Explorer" to see/run the tests
  - If you are only interested in a specific subset of the ILSpy tests, you can also use `ILSpyWpfTest` or `ILSpyWpfFrontrun`
- Use `ILSpyXplicit.dll` for the cross-platform CLI or PowerShell cmdlets
- Use `ILSpy.AddinPlugin`

# iOS emulator for Windows
jan Jones  
Faculty of Mathematics and Physics  
Charles University

## INTRODUCTION
Many developers invest their time in creating elaborate applications for Apple's iOS. What if we would be able to run these applications as they're on Windows?

### Goals
- iOS applications are compiled into ARM code; we want to run them on x86 Windows machines.
- Solution: Emulate the application's instructions. Catch calls into iOS and translate them to Windows calls.

### iOS → WINDOWS
**Problem:** How to map iOS APIs onto Windows APIs?
- Related work: Microsoft's tool Win32API has libraries posing as iOS system libraries, implemented via Windows functionality.
  - iOS app code $\rightarrow$ intercepted from source $\rightarrow$ native WIN32 app
  - iOS binaries $\rightarrow$ patched binaries $\rightarrow$ native WIN32 app
  - Other platforms are similar to what project Win32 does on Linux to enable running Windows programs.
    - Windows binary $\rightarrow$ native Linux app $\rightarrow$ Wine libraries

**Our solution:** We patched Win32API libraries to work with unmodified ARM iOS binaries.

### ARM → x86
**Problem:** We need to translate system API calls between ARM and x86 calling conventions.
- Related work: RPC (remote call) and tool SWIGs only partially implement the required translation chain.
- **Translating arbitrary APIs:**
  - RPC, SWIG, our solution
- **Our solution:** We transfer arguments through shared memory using complete-time-argument wrapper functions.

---

## RESULTS
| | iPhone | Windows |
|---|---|---|
| **Natural Execution Time** | 10 | 10 |
| **Compile Time** | 10 | 10 |
| **Platform Efficiency** | 10 | 10 |

### API THROUGHPUT BENCHMARK
- **Total**
  - Natural Execution: 1 ms

- **Function**
  - No callback: 10 ms

- **Platform**

## CONCLUSION AND FUTURE WORK
- **Conclusion:** Proof of concept works. System API call translation performs very well.
- **Future work:** Complete emulation requires a lot of iOS API implementation (mostly Win32/Win64). Adding Swift runtime would broaden the range of supported iOS apps.

# Loss Functions for Face Recognition

## A. Margin-Loss: GDis($W_1$, $W_2$) + m < GDis($X_{11}$, $X_{21}$)
- **Description**: The loss function aims to increase the distance between different classes (e.g., Class1 and Class2) by a margin `m`.
- **Formula**: $GDis(W_1, W_2) + m < GDis(X_{11}, X_{21})$
- **Visuals**:
  - $W_1$ and $W_2$ are feature vectors of the same class (e.g., all from Class1).
  - $X_{11}$ and $X_{21}$ are feature vectors of different classes.
  - The red arrow indicates the direction of increasing the inter-class distance.

## B. Intra-Loss: GDis($W_1$, $W_2$) ↓
- **Description**: The loss function aims to decrease the distance between features of the same class (intra-class).
- **Formula**: $GDis(W_1, W_2)$ is minimized.
- **Visuals**:
  - $W_1$ and $W_2$ are feature vectors of the same class (e.g., all from Class1).
  - The blue downward arrow indicates the direction of decreasing the intra-class distance.

## C. Inter-Loss: GDis($W_1$, $W_2$) ↑
- **Description**: The loss function aims to increase the distance between features of different classes (inter-class).
- **Formula**: $GDis(W_1, W_2)$ is maximized.
- **Visuals**:
  - $W_1$ and $W_2$ are feature vectors of different classes.
  - The green upward arrow indicates the direction of increasing the inter-class distance.

## D. Triplet-Loss: GDis($W_1$, $W_2$) < GDis($X_{11}$, $X_{21}$) - m
- **Description**: The loss function uses a triplet of samples: an anchor ($X_{11}$), a positive sample ($W_1$) from the same class, and a negative sample ($W_2$) from a different class. It ensures that the distance between the anchor and positive is less than the distance between the anchor and negative by a margin `m`.
- **Formula**: $GDis(W_1, W_2) < GDis(X_{11}, X_{21}) - m$
- **Visuals**:
  - $W_1$ is a feature vector of the same class as the anchor $X_{11}$.
  - $W_2$ is a feature vector of a different class from the anchor $X_{11}$.
  - The red arrow shows the required margin.

## Clustering in Embedding Space
- **Large Central Cluster**: Represents a dataset or embedding space where face images are embedded.
- **Smaller Clusters on the Right**: Represent separate groups or classes within the embedding space. These clusters are more distinct, indicating that the model has successfully learned to separate different identities.

[The image illustrates the concept of using different loss functions to learn embeddings for face recognition, where the goal is to group similar faces (same person) close together and push dissimilar faces (different people) apart in the embedding space.]

# LAStools
LiDAR processing

Award-winning software for efficient LiDAR processing (with LASzip)

## Overview
Tools for processing LiDAR data files. The data files are in ASPRS LAS format (version 1.0-1.4) or lossless compressed, otherwise, identical twin), LAS format. The table below provides information about the tools and converters provided.

LAStools consist of different parts:
- LASlib, the low-level processing API.
- LASzip, the compression/decompression API. Both parts are free and open-source.
- LAStools Software Suite. Additional tools based on LASlib and LASzip for processing LiDAR data. Some of the tools are free to use, others are licensed.
All code is written in ultra-lightweight, very efficient, and super-fast C++.

LAStools are a collection of highly efficient, multi-core batched, scriptable tools to process LAS, compressed LAZ, Terrasolid BIN, ERI Shapefiles (SHP), ASCII, and others.

The open-source part is located in \LASlib and \LASzip. The documentation is located in \bin

## Open source tools
- `laszip`: powerful lossless LiDAR compressor that turns large LAS files into much smaller LAZ files
- `lasextract`: extracts test returns, clips, subsamples, translates, etc.
- `las2txt`: turns LAS into human-readable and easy-to-parse ASCII
- `txt2las`: converts LiDAR data from ASCII text to binary LAS format
- `lasindex`: creates a spatial index LAS file for fast spatial queries
- `lasmerge`: merges several LAS or LAZ files into a single LAS or LAZ file
- `lasinfo`: prints out a quick overview of the contents of a LAS or LAZ file
- `lascopindex`: creates a COPC file for a given set of *.las or *.laz files

# WHAT IS 'LEGACYOS 2023' AND WHY IT COULD BECOME YOUR NEW OPERATING SYSTEM OF CHOICE.

## Debian
Debian proves its reliability every day in thousands of real world scenarios, ranging from single user laptops to super-colliders, stock exchanges and the automotive industry. Debian has a large number of packages (Applications and System) (currently in stable: 59000 packages). Debian package maintainers do not only take care of the Debian packaging and incorporating new upstream versions. Often they're experts on the application itself and therefore contribute to upstream development directly. Debian offers security support for its stable releases.

## antiX
antiX is a fast, lightweight and easy to install systemd-free Operating System for Intel / AMD x64 compatible systems. It is suitable for old computers. It does this by reducing system resources allowing more Processor and Memory power for Applications. antiX offers a number of unique tools designed especially for antiX.
The goal of antiX is to provide a light, but fully functional and flexible free operating system for both newcomers and experienced users.

## LegacyOS
LegacyOS takes the proven Reliability and Security of Debian and its large number of package maintainers and wraps them in a unique to LegacyOS themed Icewm Desktop. From Login to Shutdown there is a consistent feel. LegacyOS adds a large selection of Applications by default which gives the User access to Applications the average User is most likely going to need for Day to Day Tasks. OnlyOffice replaces LibreOffice, Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge can be installed from the Package Manager. Being Debian based allows access to one of if not the largest repository of Applications for Linux. Finally as LegacyOS is a Live / Install to Hard Drive Operating System and already includes all the Apps most users are going to need, LegacyOS makes a great take anywhere Bootable Live USB Stick.

# Luma3DS

**Node-proof (N)3DS "Custom Firmware"**

## What it is
Luma3DS is a program to patch the system software of (New) Nintendo (2)3DS handheld consoles "on the fly", adding features such as per-game language settings, debugging capabilities for developers, and removing restrictions enforced by Nintendo such as the region lock.

It also allows you to run unauthorized ("homebrew") content by removing signature checks. To use it, you will need a console capable of running homebrew software on the Arm9 processor.

Since v8.0, Luma3DS has its own in-game menu, triggerable by [Luma3DS] (see the release note).

## Compiling
### Prerequisites
- git
- make/rom
- i64- to-date devkitARM+libctru

1. Clone the repository with `git clone https://github.com/LumaTeam/Luma3DS.git`
2. Run `make`

The produced `boot.firm` is meant to be copied to the root of your SD card for usage with BootStrap.

## Setup / Usage / Features

# Create MATLAB variables in Julia

One can use the function `marray` to create MATLAB variables (of type `MArray`) as follows:

- `marray(Float64, n)` creates an m-by-n MATLAB zero array of double valued type
- `marray(Int32, n)` creates an m-by-n MATLAB zero array of Int32 valued type
- `marray(Bool, n)` creates a MATLAB logical array of size m-by-n
- `mcellarray(m, n)` creates a MATLAB cell array of size m-by-n
- `mstruct("a", "b", "c")` creates a MATLAB struct with given fields
- `rand(m, n)` converts a scalar 1.2 to a MATLAB variable
- `x = marray(a)` converts a Julia variable to a MATLAB array
- `sparray` converts a sparse matrix to a MATLAB sparse matrix
- `mstring` converts a string to a MATLAB char array
- `marray(["a", "b", "c"])` converts a Julia array to a MATLAB cell array
- `marray(Dict("a" => 1, "b" => "string", "c" => [1,2,3]))` converts a Julia dictionary to a MATLAB struct

The function `marray` can also convert a compound type to a Julia struct.

## Examples

```julia
struct S
    x::Float64
    y::Vector{Int32}
    z::Bool
end

s = S(1.2, [1,2,3], false)
x = marray((s, s)) # creates a MATLAB struct with three fields: x, y, z
xs = mstructarray([s, s]) # creates a MATLAB array of structs
```


# Usage ARM Linux, Windows, Linux, WebAssembly

1. Extract archive to `/project/dir/`
2. Modify `opencv_dir/Makefile.txt` to find and link opencv4

```bash
set(OpenCV_DIR ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/opencv-mobile-4.6.0-arm-linux/arm-linux-gnueabihf/lib/cmake/opencv4)
find_package(OpenCV REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(your_target ${OpenCV_LIBS})
```

## How-to-build your custom package

**step 1. download opencv source**

```bash
wget -q https://github.com/opencv/opencv/archive/4.6.0.zip -O opencv-4.6.0.zip
unzip -q opencv-4.6.0.zip
cd opencv-4.6.0
```

**step 2. strip zlib dependency and use stb-based highgui implementation (optional)**

```bash
patch -p1 -i ../opencv-4.6.0-no-zlib.patch
truncat -s 0 cmake/Opencv4IndLibsRtst.cmake
rm -rf modules/gapi
cp -r .../Highgui modules/
```

**step 3. patch opencv source for no-rtti build (optional)**

```bash
patch -p1 -i ../opencv-4.6.0-no-rtti.patch
```

**step 4. apply your opencv options to opencv4_cmake_options.txt**

**step 5. build your opencv package with cmake**

```bash
mkdir -p build
cd build
cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=install \
-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
-CT ..\opencv4_cmake_options.txt \ 
-DBUILD_opencv_world=OFF
```

**step 6. make a package**

```bash
zip -r opencv-mobile-4.6.0.zip install
```

# overlay-amd64-openfyde

## Introduction

Same as Chromium OS, openFyde adopts the Portage build and packaging system from Gentoo Linux. openFyde uses Portage with certain customizations to support building multiple targets (bootable OS system images) across different hardware architectures from a shared set of sources.

A board defines a target type, it can be either a family of hardware devices or specifically for one type of device. For example, the board `amd64/4064` architecture is a target type for an openFyde system image that aims to run on most recent PCs with amd64/4064 architecture whilst the `fyde4064` board is a target type specifically for the infamous single-board computer Raspberry Pi 4. We usually append `_openfyde` to the board name in openFyde to differentiate between the siblings for FydeOS.

Each board has a corresponding overlay that defines the configuration for this. It includes details like CPU architecture, kernel configuration, as well as additional packages and USE flags.

## About this repository

This repository is the overlay for the `amd64-openfyde` board, it's a part of the openFyde open-source project.

This repository contains the following packages:

| Packages | Description | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| `chromeos-base/device-appid` | Setup device appid | `amd64-openfyde` board setup |
| `chromeos-base/amd64-openfyde-spec` | `amd64-openfyde` board setup | |
| `media-libs/pep-support-blacklist` | Files used to support/configure LPE Audio | `chromiums-overlay` |
| `virtual/fydeos-board-spec-dev` | Virtual for fydeos board setup | |
| `virtual/openfyde-board-spec` | Virtual for openFyde dev board setup | |
| `virtual/arc-camera3-hal-configs` | `suplous` camera config | |
| `virtual/arc-camera3-hal` | `cros usb camera hal` | |

# Air Fryer BBQ Chicken Tenders

**Source:** `https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/272658/air-fryer-bbq-chicken-tenders/`

**Servings:** 6 serving(s)

**Total Time:** 40 minutes

**Rating:** 0

**Description:** Homemade barbecue-crusted chicken tenders in an air fryer. Crispy on the outside, tender on the inside, and no flipping required.

---

### Ingredients:

- 3 ½ ounces barbecue-flavored pork rinds
- 1 cup all-purpose flour
- 1 tablespoon barbecue seasoning
- 1 egg, beaten
- 1 ½ pounds chicken breast tenderloins
- cooking spray

---

### Instructions:

**Step 1** Preheat an air fryer to 370 degrees F (190 degrees C). Advertisement  
**Step 2** Place pork rinds in a food processor and pulse to the size of bread crumbs. Place in a shallow bowl. Mix flour and barbecue seasoning together in a shallow dish. Beat egg in a third shallow bowl.  
**Step 3** Coat each chicken tender first in the flour mixture, then dip in beaten egg, and finally coat in pork rind crumbs.  
**Step 4** Spray the basket of the air fryer with nonstick cooking spray. Arrange 1/2 of the chicken tenders in the air fryer basket, making sure none are touching. Spray the top of each tender with cooking spray. Cook until chicken is cooked through and no longer pink at the center, about 15 minutes. Repeat with remaining tenders.

Popcorn TimeTV was an Apple TV, iPhone and iPad application to torrent movies and tv shows for streaming.

Since 2016, this project has grown exponentially - both in its user base and in its functionality. However, the team has since gone the other way. We went from having 13 developers on the team to 1 developer and 1 designer, both of whom have lives and projects outside of Popcorn Time. We have decided that we have given all this to the project and it's time for us to move on to pursue greater things. There is no doubt that this comes with a heavy heart as we have learned so much from this project and watched it grow from this simple torrenting app which could only play 720p video, to what it is today.

All that being said, we do not want this project to just die off as we leave. The size of the project might be a bit daunting to an unassessed developer, but the app is extremely stable and packed with almost every feature you could need, so unless you're planning on doing a rewrite, it should be OK.

# Project Description

SharpKeys is a utility that manages a Registry key that allows Windows to remap one key to any other key. Included in the application is a list of common Registry keys and Type Key feature to automatically recognize most keyboard keys. It was originally developed in C# using .NET v2 but has been updated to support .NET 4.0 Client Profile.

## Original Mission

This is something I’ve thrown together to help people out with their keyboard mappings. What’s a keyboard mapping? How many times a day do you accidentally hit Caps Lock by MISTAKE and END UP HAVING TO GO BACK and retype stuff? For me it was at least once an hour – in fact, I used to pop off the Caps Lock key so I wouldn’t hit it anymore, and Windows 10. There’s a little used registry hack that allows you to remap keys across a keyboard. For me, this meant that I told my computer to treat Caps Lock as if it were a Shift key, which I now have.

When I first started working with other keyboards, the more I wanted to have this ability to map other keys across my keyboard. But working with the finer numbers and having too look up scan codes could be painful, hence SharpKeys.

SharpKeys is not responsible for any of the keyboard remapping functionality – it simply exposes a Registry key that controls how Windows remaps keys and has been available since Windows 2000. The list of keys that are included in the application are from most of the US-based keyboards that I’ve used over the years and is not guaranteed to be 100% complete for world keyboards.

### Manual via web or Microsoft Store

Click the `Installer` button in the header above or get the same MSI from the Microsoft Store.

Note: for that ARM versions of Windows, please use the ZIP file to get the EXE; the MSI is looking for x64/x86.

#### winget

If you are using WinGet and want to install the MSI from GitHub:

```bash
winget install -e RandyKraut.SharpKeys
```

Likewise you can also install the Microsoft Store version of the app via WinGet by

```bash
winget install -e XPF6G76673D4F
```

### Group: Spotify

- **Snapdroid**: Mobile app interface for controlling the Spotify group.

### Group: MPD
- **Snapdroid / Snapweb**: Interface for controlling the MPD group.
- **Snapclient**: Runs on various platforms including Linux (represented by Tux), Android, Chrome OS, and Windows.

- **Communication**: Data flows from the Snapserver to clients via TCP or Websocket.

# SoftEther VPN Architecture Diagram

The diagram illustrates the architecture of the SoftEther VPN system, showing various components and their interconnections.

## Components and Connections

### Clients
- **SoftEther VPN Client** at Home:
  - Connects via a **VPN Tunnel** over TCP/UDP.
  - The tunnel terminates at the Virtual Hub.
- **SoftEther VPN Client** in a Hotel room:
  - Connects via a **VPN Tunnel** over TCP/UDP.
  - The tunnel terminates at the Virtual Hub.
- **Built-in VPN clients** on Smartphones:
  - Connect via a **VPN Tunnel** over TCP/UDP.
  - The tunnel terminates at the Virtual Hub.

### Core Network Components
- **Virtual Hub** (at Headquarters):
  - Acts as a central point for all incoming VPN tunnels.
  - Connected to a **Physical Ethernet Adapter (Local Bridging)**.
  - The adapter is connected to a **Physical Ethernet Switch**.
- **Remote Virtual Hub** (at Branch Offices):
  - Serves as a local hub for branch office devices.
  - Connected to a **Physical Ethernet Adapter (Local Bridging)**.
  - The adapter is connected to a **Physical Ethernet Switch**.

### Network Infrastructure
- **Existing Servers and PCs**:
  - Located at Headquarters and Branch Offices.
  - Connected to the network through the Physical Ethernet Switches.
- **Physical Ethernet Switches**:
  - At both Headquarters and Branch Offices.
  - Connect the physical network to the virtual network via the Local Bridging adapters.

### Key Features
- **Cascading**:
  - A connection between the main Virtual Hub and the Remote Virtual Hub.
  - Allows for a hierarchical or layered network structure, enabling remote access to the main network.
- **Local Bridging**:
  - Enables the integration of the virtual network with the existing physical network.
  - The Physical Ethernet Adapters allow the Virtual Hub to act as a bridge, making the virtual network appear as part of the physical LAN.

## Summary of Data Flow
1.  **Client Connection**: Users at Home, in a Hotel, or on their smartphones use the SoftEther VPN Client to establish a secure **VPN Tunnel**.
2.  **Tunnel Termination**: The tunnel connects to the **Virtual Hub** at the headquarters.
3.  **Network Integration**: The Virtual Hub uses a **Physical Ethernet Adapter** to perform **Local Bridging**, connecting the virtual network to the **Physical Ethernet Switch**.
4.  **Access to Resources**: The **Physical Ethernet Switch** provides access to the **Existing Servers and PCs** on the local network.
5.  **Branch Office Access**: The **Remote Virtual Hub** at a branch office allows local users to connect. It is linked to the main Virtual Hub via **Cascading**, allowing it to be managed as part of the larger network.

This architecture enables secure, remote access to a company's internal network from any location, while maintaining the security and control of a traditional local area network (LAN).

## Arch Linux
You can install Suwamoyi from the AUR.
```bash
yay -S tachidisk
```

## Debian/Ubuntu
Download the latest deb package from the release section or install from the MPR.
```bash
git clone https://git.madeb.org/suwayomi/suwayomi-server.git
cd suwayomi-server
make build
```

## Ubuntu
```bash
sudo add-apt-repository ppa:suwayomi/suwayomi-server
sudo apt update
sudo apt install suwayomi-server
```

## Docker
Check our Official Docker release [Suwayomi Container](https://hub.docker.com/r/suwayomi/suwayomi) for running Suwamoyi Server in a docker container. Source code is available at [docker.tachidisk.io](https://docker.tachidisk.io). By default, the server will be running on `http://localhost:4567`.

Install from the command line:
```bash
$ docker pull gcr.io/suwayomi/tachidisk
```

Run Container from the command line:
```bash
$ docker run -p 4567:4567 gcr.io/suwayomi/tachidisk
```

# TERMINATOR(1)

## NAME
Terminator - Multiple GNOME terminals in one window

## SYNOPSIS
terminator [options]

## DESCRIPTION
This manual pages documents that allows users to set up flexible arrangements of GNOME terminals (it is aimed at those who normally arrange lots of terminals near each other, and don't want to use a frame-based window manager).

This program follows the usual GNU command line syntax, with long options starting with two dashes ('--'). A summary of options is included below.

## OPTIONS
- `-h`, `--help`  
  Show summary of options
- `-v`, `--version`  
  Show the version of the Terminator installation
- `-m`, `--maximize`  
  Start with a maximised window
- `-f`, `--fullscreen`  
  Start with a fullscreen window
- `-b`, `--borderless`  
  Instruct the Terminator window not to render borders/decoration on the Terminator window (this window by default. Its visibility can be toggled with the hide/enable keyboard shortcut (Ctrl+Shift+Alt+o) with default)
- `-H`, `--hide`  
  Hide the Terminator window by default. Its visibility can be toggled with the hide/enable keyboard shortcut (Ctrl+Shift+Alt+o) with default
- `-T`, `--title`  
  Force the Terminator window to use a specific name rather than the operating system's name for the child shell.

# test(1)

## NAME
test - Evaluate conditional expression

## SYNOPSIS
test [expresion]

## DESCRIPTION
Exits with a status of 0 (true) or 1 (false) depending on the evaluation of EXPRESSION. Valid expressions may be examined by the status of a file. There are string operators and numeric comparison operators as well.

The behavior of test depends on the number of arguments. Read the bash operators page for the complete specification.

| File operators | | |
|----------------|---|---|
| `-c FILE`      | True if file exists and is a character special. | |
| `-d FILE`      | True if file exists and is a directory. | |
| `-e FILE`      | True if file exists. | |
| `-f FILE`      | True if file exists and is a regular file. | |
| `-g FILE`      | True if file exists and has its set-group-id bit set. | |
| `-r FILE`      | True if file exists and is readable. | |
| `-s FILE`      | True if file exists and has size greater than zero. | |
| `-t N`         | True if file descriptor N is open and refers to a terminal. | |
| `-u FILE`      | True if file exists and has its set-user-id bit set. | |
| `-w FILE`      | True if file exists and is writable. | |
| `-x FILE`      | True if file exists and is executable. | |
| `-z STRING`    | True if string is empty. | |
| `-n STRING`    | True if string is not empty. | |
| `STRING1 = STRING2` | True if strings are equal. | |
| `STRING1 != STRING2` | True if strings are not equal. | |
| `STRING1 < STRING2` | True if string1 is lexicographically less than string2. | |
| `STRING1 > STRING2` | True if string1 is lexicographically greater than string2. | |
| `NUM1 -eq NUM2` | True if num1 is numerically equal to num2. | |
| `NUM1 -ne NUM2` | True if num1 is numerically not equal to num2. | |
| `NUM1 -lt NUM2` | True if num1 is numerically less than num2. | |
| `NUM1 -le NUM2` | True if num1 is numerically less than or equal to num2. | |
| `NUM1 -gt NUM2` | True if num1 is numerically greater than num2. | |
| `NUM1 -ge NUM2` | True if num1 is numerically greater than or equal to num2. | |

# tiny11builder

Scripts to build a trimmed-down Windows 11 image - now in PowerShell!

Tiny11 builder, now completely overhauled.

After more than a year (for which I'm also sorry), tiny11 is now a much more complete and flexible solution - one script fits all. Also, it's a steppingstone for an even more fleshed-out solution.
You can now use it on ANY Windows 11 release (not just a specific build), as well as any AMY language or architecture.
You can make it possible thanks to the much-improved scripting capabilities of PowerShell, compared to the older Batch release.

Since it is written in PowerShell, you need to set the execution policy to Unrestricted so that you could run the script. If you haven't done this before, make sure to run Set-ExecutionPolicy Unrestricted as administrator in PowerShell before running the script, otherwise it will just crash.

This script created to automate the build of a streamlined Windows 11 image, similar to tiny11. My main goal is to use only Microsoft utilities (DISM, and no utilities from external sources). The only executable included in existing.exe, which is provided in the Windows ADK and is used to create bootable ISO images. Also included is an unattended answer file, which is used to bypass Microsoft Account on OOBE and to deploy the image with the /accepteula flag. It's open-source, so feel free to add or remove anything you want! Feedback is also much appreciated.

Also, for the very first time, introducing tiny11 core builder! A more powerful script, designed for a quick and dirty development testbed. Just the bare minimum, none of the fluff. This script generates a significantly reduced Windows 11 image. It's not meant to be used due to lack of serializability, it can't add packages, updates, or features post-VM environments. Tiny11 Core is not a full Windows 11 substitute but a rapid testing or development tool, potentially useful for VM environments.

## Instructions:

1. Download Windows 11 from the Microsoft website ([https://www.microsoft.com/software-download/windows11](https://www.microsoft.com/software-download/windows11))
2. Mount the downloaded ISO image using Windows Explorer.
3. Select the drive letter where the image is mounted (only the letter, no color!)
4. Select the SKU that you want the image to be based.
5. Sit back and relax.
6. When the image is completed, you will see it in the folder where the script was extracted, with the name tiny11.so

## Options

| Optional Argument | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `-h`, `--help` | show this help message and exit |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | explain what is being done, duplicate for more verbosity (default: 1) |
| `-s`, `--silent` | no non-essential output. |
| `-l`, `--list` | list the contents of the archive(s) in a flat list. |

| Advanced Argument | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--continue-on-error` | try to continue extraction when something goes wrong. |
| `-f VERSION`, `--force VERSION` | ignore the archive header and assume this exact version. Possible versions: RPA-1.0, RPA-2.0, RPA-3.0, ALT-1.0, ZDX-1.2A, ZDX-2.0, RPA-3.2, RPA-4.0. |

# Download the best video-only format and the best audio-only format without merging them
# For this case, an output template should be used since
# by default, both video and bortaosts will have the same file name.
yt-dlp -f "bv+ba" -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s"  # or: -f "bv+ba"

# Download and merge the best format that has a video stream,
# and all audio-only formats into one file
yt-dlp -f "bv+mergeall:audio"  # or: -f "bv+mergesingle:audio"

# Download and merge the best format that has a video stream,
# and the best 2 audio-only formats into one file

## Notepads App

A modern, lightweight text editor with a minimalist design.

### What is Notepads and why do I care?

I have been waiting long enough for a modern Windows 10 notepad app to come so I decide to create one myself. Don't get me wrong, Notepad++, VS Code, etc., are great but they are too heavy.

So here comes the "Notepads" (s stands for Sets).

- Fluent design with a built-in tab system.
- Blazing fast and lightweight.
- Launch from the command line or PowerShell by typing: `notepads` or `notepads %FilePath%`.
- Multi-line handwriting support.
- Built-in Markdown live preview.
- Built-in diff viewer (preview your changes).
- Session snapshot and multi-instances.

# Super UEFIinSecureBoot Disk

## Features
- GRUB2 Bootloader
- 32-bit (a32) / 64-bit (e64) EFI (+ Secure Boot support)
- BIOS / UEFI CSM support
- Launch any operating system
- Launch any .efi executable from GRUB2
- Launch any .efi executable from another .efi application
- Load any UEFI drivers

## Based on:
- Red Hat Shim (v15.8), from Fedora, signed with Microsoft key, for initial boot
- Modified Linux Foundation Preloader to install circumventing UEFI Security Policy
- GRUB2 with security bypass patches by chainloader, linux/linxuef and shim

## Description
Secure Boot is a feature of UEFI firmware which is designed to secure the boot process by preventing the loading of drivers or OS loaders that are not signed with an acceptable digital signature.

Most modern computers come with Secure Boot enabled by default, which is a requirement for Windows 10 certification process. Although it could be disabled in UEFI setup menu, sometimes it's not easily possible to do, due to UEFI setup password in a corporate laptop where the user doesn't have administrative rights.

This disk, after being installed on a USB flash drive and booted from, effectively disables Secure Boot protection features and temporary allows to perform almost all actions with the PC as if Secure Boot is disabled. This could be useful for data recovery, OS re-installation, or just for booting from USB without thinking about additional steps.

## Installation
Download image file from releases page, write it to USB flash drive using one of the following programs:

- [Rufus](https://rufus.ie/) (for Windows and Linux)
- [Etcher](https://www.balena.io/etcher/) (for Windows, Linux and macOS)

**WARNING:** all your USB flash data will be deleted.

The image contains single FAT32 500MB partition. Use gparted or similar tool to resize it to get full USB drive space.

# Installation

The easiest way to install clamtk is to use the rpms. The commands `dnf` and `yum` will pull in requirements.

First, start with the official repositories.
```bash
sudo yum install clamtk or sudo dnf install clamtk
```

If this does not work, download the file from the [official site](https://www.clamtk.org/). You should be able to just double click the file for installation or upgrade.

For these examples, we will use version 6.17. The name of the file may differ based on your distribution.

To install using a terminal window:
```bash
sudo rpm -i clamtk-6.17-1.el9.noarch.rpm or sudo dnf install clamtk-6.17-1.fc39.noarch.rpm
```

To remove clamtk:
```bash
sudo yum erase clamtk or sudo dnf erase clamtk
```

## Source

**Warning:** Don't do this. It's much easier to just double click a .deb or .rpm. Really, put down the source.

The tarball contains all the sources. One way to do this, as tested on Fedora, is to run the following commands:
```bash
tar -xf clamtk-6.17.tar.xz
sudo mkdir -p /usr/share/perl5/vendor_perl/ClamTk
sudo cp 1lib/*pm /usr/share/perl5/vendor_perl/ClamTk
sudo chown -R root:root /usr/share/perl5/vendor_perl/ClamTk
sudo cp clambd /usr/local/bin/ (or /usr/bin/)
```

Examples:
```bash
perl clamtk
```
```bash
chmod +x /path/to/clamtk
/path/to/clamtk
```

* If you have installed this program as an rpm or .deb, you do not need to take these steps.

# fping

-4, --ipv4
  Restrict name resolution and IPs to IPv4 addresses.

-6, --ipv6
  Restrict name resolution and IPs to IPv6 addresses.

-a, --alive
  Show systems that are alive.

-A, --addr
  Display targets by address rather than onm name. Combined with -d, the output will be both the ip and (if available) the hostname.

-b, --size=bytes
  Number of bytes of ping data to send. The minimum size (normally 12) allows room for the data needs to do its work (sequence number, timestamp). The reported received data size includes the ip header (normally 20 bytes) and icmp header (8 bytes), so the minimum total size is 40 bytes. Default is 56, as in ping. Maximum is the theoretical maximum ip datagram size (64k), though most systems limit this to a smaller, system-dependent number.

-B, --backoff-factor
  In the default mode, fping sends several requests to a target before giving up, waiting longer for a reply on each successive request. This parameter is the value by which the wait time is multiplied on each successive request; it must be entered as a floating-point number (x.y). The default is 1.5.

-C, --count
  Number of request packets to send to each target. In this mode, a line is displayed for each received response (this can suppressed with -q or -Q). Also, statistics about responses for each target are displayed when all requests have been sent (or when interrupted).

-C, --vcount=N
  Similar to -C, but the per-target statistics are displayed in a format designed for automated response-time statistics gathering. For example:
  $ fping -C 5 -q somehost
  somehost : 91.7 37.0 29.2 - 36.8
  shows the response time in milliseconds for each of the five requests, with the -- indicating no response was received to the fourth request.

## LA 10-Day Trip Itinerary for 3 People (Less Crowded, Food & Culture-Focused)

### Day 1: Arrival & Southern California Culture
1. **Morning:** Arrive in LA; check into a boutique hotel in Silver Lake or Arts District (less touristy than Downtown).
2. **Afternoon:** Explore Echo Park for art galleries, vegan cafes, and the Echo Park Lake. Visit the Chinatown (less crowded than the main area) for a quiet walk and local food.
3. **Evening:** Dinner at Taco Santa (a hidden gem in the Eastside) or Olive Garden (a casual spot in a quieter area).

### Day 2: Santa Monica & Beach Culture
1. **Morning:** Visit Santa Monica Pier (early morning to avoid crowds), then stroll along the Santa Monica Beach.
2. **Afternoon:** Explore Catalina Ferry (short boat trip to the island for a peaceful day).
3. **Evening:** Dinner at Cocina de Mexico (a local Mexican eatery in Santa Monica).

### Day 3: Hollywood & Entertainment
1. **Morning:** Visit the Getty Center (free admission, less crowded early morning).
2. **Afternoon:** Explore the Hollywood Walk of Fame and Grauman's Chinese Theatre.
3. **Evening:** Dinner at The Ivy (a trendy restaurant with a cozy ambiance).

### Day 4: Beverly Hills & Luxury Shopping
1. **Morning:** Browse Rodeo Drive for luxury shopping.
2. **Afternoon:** Visit the Beverly Hills Hotel & Spa for a leisurely lunch.
3. **Evening:** Dinner at Spago (a renowned Italian-American restaurant).

### Day 5: Downtown LA & Urban Exploration
1. **Morning:** Explore the Arts District with its street art and galleries.
2. **Afternoon:** Visit the Grand Central Market for diverse food options.
3. **Evening:** Dinner at Republique (a French bistro known for its desserts).

### Day 6: Malibu & Coastal Beauty
1. **Morning:** Drive to Malibu for scenic views and beach time.
2. **Afternoon:** Visit the Malibu Wine Trail for wine tasting.
3. **Evening:** Dinner at The Cottage (a rustic seafood restaurant).

### Day 7: Pasadena & Cultural Attractions
1. **Morning:** Visit the Huntington Library & Gardens.
2. **Afternoon:** Explore Old Town Pasadena for shopping and dining.
3. **Evening:** Dinner at The Blue Plate (a classic American diner).

### Day 8: Anaheim & Theme Parks
1. **Morning:** Visit Disneyland Resort (early arrival to minimize crowds).
2. **Afternoon:** Explore Disney California Adventure Park.
3. **Evening:** Dinner at California Grill (located at the Disneyland Hotel).

### Day 9: Venice Beach & Bohemian Vibes
1. **Morning:** Explore Venice Beach Boardwalk for street performers and vendors.
2. **Afternoon:** Visit the Venice Canals for a serene walk.
3. **Evening:** Dinner at The Lobster Bar (a seafood-focused restaurant).

### Day 10: Relaxation & Departure
1. **Morning:** Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at a local café.
2. **Afternoon:** Pack up and prepare for departure.
3. **Evening:** Final dinner at a favorite spot from the trip.

  - `OPS="1234567890,8967654321"`
- **MEMBERS** is used to define the members on the server.
  - `MEMBERS="1234567890,8967654321"`
- **VISITORS** is used to define visitor on the server.
  - `VISITORS="1234567890,8967654321"`

## Willkommen bei Microsoft Office Outlook 2003
Outlook 2003-Team [olteam@microsoft.com]

### RTF | Plain Text ✅ Fixed Font

Herzlich willkommen bei Microsoft® Office Outlook® 2003! Die neuen Features dieser Outlook-Version wurden speziell dafür konzipiert, Ihnen beim Verwalten des E-Mail-Stroms zu helfen und Sie beim Zeit-Management zu unterstützen.

Wir haben eine Liste unserer besten neuen Features zusammengestellt, um Ihnen einen Eindruck zu geben, was Outlook 2003 zu bieten hat.

---

**Optimierter Umgang mit E-Mail.** Mit Outlook können Sie jetzt Nachrichten besser lesen, einfacher kategorisieren und zur Nachverfolgung kennzeichnen und schneller finden. Das neue Fensterlayout zeigt mehr Informationen auf dem Bildschirm an, sogar auf kleineren Bildschirmen. Die Nachrichtenliste wurde neu gestaltet, damit die Benutzeroberfläche besser auszunutzen ist und das Scrollen zu minimieren. Nachrichten werden automatisch gruppiert, damit Sie Nachrichten in der Nachrichtenliste schneller finden. Sie können sogar alle Nachrichten in einer Gruppe auf einmal löschen oder verschieben.

**Junk-E-Mail-Filter.** Mit dem neuen Junk-E-Mail-Filter wird ein Großteil der unerwünschten E-Mail ausgefiltert. Der von Microsoft Research entwickelte Filter verwendet z.B. die Sendezzeit und den Inhalt der Nachrichten, um auszuwerten, ob eine Nachricht Junk-E-Mail ist. Aufgrund von erweiterten Analysen der Nachrichtenstruktur wird die Wahrscheinlichkeit ermittelt, mit der es sich bei einer Nachricht um Junk-E-Mail handelt. Jede vom Filter als Junk-E-Mail ausgewertete Nachricht wird in den Junk-E-Mail-Ordner verschoben. Sie können E-Mail-Adressen zu Liste sicherer Absender hinzufügen, damit Nachrichten von diesen Absendern nicht als Junk-E-Mail behandelt werden. Nachrichten von diesen Absendern werden blockiert, indem Sie Absender oder Domänen blockieren, indem Sie Absender über Listeblocker-Absender hinzufügen.

**Der Navigationsbereich.** Der Navigationsbereich vereint die zentralen Navigations- und Freigabefunktionen auf einer benutzerfreundlichen Leiste. Im Nachrichtenmodul sehen Sie mehr E-Mail-Ordner als zuvor, und Sie können Ihre Lieblingsordner ganz oben in der Liste anzeigen. Im Kalendermodul können Sie die freigegebenen Kalender anderer Personen neben Ihnen eigenen im Netz. Darüber hinaus gibt es neue, verbesserte Ansichten auf Ihre Kontaktinformationen. Alle acht Outlook-Module sind individuell und trotzdem konsistent gestaltet, damit Sie sich schnell zurechtfinden und im Handumdrehen finden können was Sie suchen, auf eine Art, die Sie persönlich anspricht.

**Der Lesebereich.** Ideal zum Lesen von Nachrichten ohne ein neues Fenster öffnen zu müssen. Das vertikale Layout des Lesebereichs in Form eines Blatts Papier ist angehmen für die Augen, und zusammen mit dem mehrzeiligen Nachrichtensehen sehen Sie auf einem gleich großen Bildschirm nun fast doppelt so viel vom Nachrichteninhalt wie mit dem Vorschaufenster in der letzten Version von Outlook.

# Open source version of the STMicroelectronics STLINK Tools

Recent features and bugfixes can be found in the [Changelog](https://github.com/stlink-org/stlink/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) of this software project.

License  
The stlink library and tools are licensed under the **BSD-3 License**.

## Introduction

stlink is an open source toolset to program and debug STM32 devices and boards manufactured by STMicroelectronics. It supports several so called "STLink" programmer boards (and clones thereof) which use a microcontroller chip to translate commands from USB to JTAG/SWD. There are four generations available on the market, all are supported by this toolset:

*   **STLINK/V1** (obsolete as of 21-11-2019, continued support by this toolset)
    *   transport layer: SCSI passthru commands over USB
    *   stand-alone programmer
    *   on-board on STM32VL Discovery boards
*   **STLINK/V2**
    *   transport layer: raw USB commands
    *   stand-alone programmer
    *   on-board on STM32L Discovery and STM32 Nucleo boards
*   **STLINK/V2-1**
    *   transport layer: raw USB commands
    *   on-board on some STM32 Nucleo boards
*   **STLINK/V3**
    *   transport layer: raw USB commands
    *   stand-alone programmer (STLINK-V3SET, STLINK-V3MINI, STLINK-V3MODS)
    *   on-board on some STM32 Nucleo boards (STLINK-V3)

On the user level there is no difference in handling or operation between these different revisions.

The STLink toolset includes:
*   `st-info` - a programmer and chip information tool
*   `st-flash` - a flash manipulation tool
*   `st-trace` - a logging tool to record information on execution
*   `st-util` - a GDB server (supported in Visual Studio Code / VSCode via the Cortex-Debug plugin)
*   `st-link` - a communication library
*   `st-link-gui` - a GUI interface (optional)

# Vanilla OS Live ISO Builder

This ISO builder is a combination of previous efforts from Ubuntu Budgie (Budgee remix at the time), some stuff from livecd-tools from launchpad, and thanks to the amazing devs from all around Elem Link.
https://github.com/elementary/os

## Building Locally

1.  Clone this project & cd into it.
    ```bash
    git clone https://github.com/Vanilla-OS/live-iso.git && cd live-iso
    ```
2.  Configure the channel in the `<tt>etc/tarvers.conf</tt>` file (unstable, all).
3.  Run the build:
    ```bash
    docker run --privileged -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock -v ${PWD}:/working_dir -w /working_dir gher.io/vanilla-os/pico:main /bin/bash -c "cd /working_dir && ./build.sh"
    ```
4.  When done, your image will be in the `builds` folder.
